column5: CRA 2015 s9: goods must be of satisfactory quality, judged by what a reasonable person would consider satisfactory taking account of the description, the price and all other relevant circumstances; quality includes appearance and finish, freedom from minor defects, safety and durability; the term does not cover anything that makes quality unsatisfactory which was specifically drawn to the consumer's attention before the contract, or which an examination the consumer made ought to have revealed. Replaces the course's 'our reading' line: disclosing a flaw before sale legally removes it from a quality claim, which is why a full flaw list protects the seller.

CRA 2015 s2: a trader acts for purposes of their trade, business, craft or profession; a consumer is an individual acting wholly or mainly outside theirs, and a trader who says otherwise must prove it; second-hand goods sold at a public auction that individuals can attend in person fall outside most of the goods chapter (except sections 11(4)-(5), 12, 28 and 29).

CRA 2015 s11 and s12: goods must match their description, and the main-characteristics information given under the Consumer Contracts Regulations (and other required pre-contract information) becomes a term of the contract that cannot be changed unless expressly agreed. So the listing text is part of the contract.

CRA 2015 s17: the trader must have the right to sell the goods, and they must be free of undisclosed charges; breach gives a right to reject (s19(6)). Supports the course's 'right to sell: source recorded' checklist row.

CRA 2015 s19-s24 remedies: short-term right to reject within 30 days of delivery (s22); then one repair or replacement at the trader's cost including postage (s23); then a price reduction or final right to reject (s24), with no deduction for use in the first 6 months except for motor vehicles; a fault appearing within 6 months of delivery is presumed to have been there at delivery unless the trader shows otherwise (s19(14)-(15)). The refund must be paid within 14 days of the trader agreeing it, by the same payment method, with no fee, and the trader bears reasonable costs of returning rejected goods (s20). Module 6 mentions only the 14-day cancellation and 'not as described' in general.

CRA 2015 s28-s29: unless agreed otherwise, the trader must deliver without undue delay and within 30 days; goods remain at the trader's risk until they come into the physical possession of the consumer (or someone they name), unless the consumer commissions a carrier the trader did not offer. So damage in the post is the seller's risk, a strong reason for the packing standards in module 6.

CRA 2015 s31: a contract term is not binding on the consumer so far as it would exclude or restrict liability under sections 9 to 17, 28 or 29, or make remedies subject to onerous conditions. Confirms the course's callout that 'sold as seen' or 'no returns' wording cannot remove these rights for a trader selling to a consumer.
